digest.component_or_area: Git fetch coordination in store sync and snapshot paths
propositions: Parallel rebar operations that run Git fetches against a shared Git common directory without coordination fail with 'cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/tickets: is at <new> but expected <old>' because remote-tracking refs are updated via compare-and-swap semantics and uncoordinated processes observe stale refs

The sync fetch path (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) runs fetches outside the store write lock before taking it, and neither sync nor snapshot fetch paths coordinate through the per-worktree Git advisory lock, leaving a race condition when multiple worktrees or the shared tickets clone update the same remote-tracking ref

Controlled experiments demonstrate the stale-reference comparison failure reproduces reliably in parallel execution (82/128 attempts) but never occurs in serialized execution, confirming the race is a coordination defect

The fix requires a blocking cross-process fetch lock keyed on the canonical Git common directory identity, bounded retry for residual races with non-rebar Git peers, and preservation of fetch execution outside the ticket write lock to avoid blocking local writers on remote I/O
